newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks edge higher after breather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks edge higher after breather.

text.p: Stocks rose slightly Friday after pausing to consolidate recent sharp gains amid weakness in pharmaceutical and certain technology stocks.

At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial average was up 9.75 points, or 0.12 percent, at 8,126.68. Advancers were slightly ahead of decliners on volume of 312 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index also edged higher, up 2.11 points, or 0.13 percent, at 1,571.24.
"There is lots of volatility as the stock market digests its recent volatile gains," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "This kind of volatility is to be expected."

Stocks deserved to take a breath after pushing to new highs earlier this week, analysts said. They had been lifted by strong corporate earnings and upbeat congressional testimony on the economy by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 1/32, or 31.25 cents on a $1,000 bond, and its yield of 6.44 percent was unchanged.
The broader markets were also higher, although stocks of both drug markers and personal computer companies fell.

"The drug stocks are weak," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp., said. "Two announcments -- Bristol losing a patent case and Pfizer Inc. forecasting single-digit growth in the second half -- knocked them back."
Pfizer's stock tumbled 3-3/4 to 58 after the company said it expects earnings for the second half of 1997 to grow in single digits over the same period last year.

Stock in Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. lost 15/16 to 81-5/8. Norwegian pharmaceuticals company Nycomed ASA said a court in The Hague ruled against Bristol's claim of patent infringement against Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals.
Stock in Dow components Merck & Co. and Johnson and Johnson were weaker.
Personal computer maker stocks also slipped from recent sharp highs. Dell Computer Corp. lost 7 to 163 and Compaq Computer Corp. shed 4-1/2 to 136.
"When stocks like this reverse, they make an equally fervent move on the donwside," Bleier said.

Stein said there was concern Gateway 2000 Inc. was planning to make more inroads into the corporate computer market. Gateway stock was down 2-15/16 at 41. It earned 36 cents a share in the second quarter, compared with 33 cents a year ago.
Among economic data, durable goods orders for June rose 2.3 percent, and existing home sales slipped 2.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted rate of 4.14 million units.

"All of the news lately, including the earnings and the numbers today, look pretty good," Barbara Marcin, vice president, Citibank Global Asset Management, said, adding that the stock market was consolidating slightly.
Silicon Graphics Inc. rose 5-11/16 to 25-1/8. It posted an above-forecast fourth-quarter profit of 56 cents per share, compared with a year-ago loss of 30 cents per share.
Bear Stearns & Co. Inc., Goldman, Sachs and Co., Cowen, Hambrecht & Quist and Salomon all raised their rating on the stock.
Columbia/HCA stock gained 12/16 to 36-15/16. It said its chairman and chief executive, Richard Scott, and its president and chief operating officer, David Vandewater, had resigned.
